chunks: And Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn 'Uqda narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yusuf ibn Ya'qub al-Ja'fi, Abu al-Hasan, narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Mihran narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza narrated to us, from Abdul A'la ibn A'yun, saying: Abu Abdullah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them) said to me:

O Abdul A'la, undertaking our matter is not merely knowing it and accepting it. Undertaking our matter is preserving it and concealing it from those who are not of its people. So convey to them my greeting and the mercy of Allah - meaning the Shia - and say to them: He says to you: May Allah have mercy upon a servant who draws the love of people to himself and to us by showing them what they know and refraining from them what they deny. (Then he said) One who makes war against us is not more burdensome than the one who speaks against us with what we dislike.

key_terms.النَّاصِبُ: The one who sets up war/hostility against

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between knowing the Imamate and undertaking it according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In the era of the Minor Occultation, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates *ihtimal* (bearing/undertaking) beyond mere intellectual acceptance to include *sitr* (concealment), emphasizing the strategic preservation of the Imamate's sanctity from the unqualified. This principle of *tajalli* (manifestation) and *istirrar* (concealment) guides the Shia to display familiar truths to win hearts while hiding esoteric realities from those who would distort them, a tactic deemed more taxing than open warfare. This reflects the broader Shia doctrine of *Taqiyya* as a dynamic tool for communal survival and theological integrity during periods of political persecution.
